A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Abstract Gradient Training (AGT) research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original AGT certification experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, together with empirical poisoning-attack studies in Appendix H.

after.justification: v3 retains original certification and poisoning-attack results and adds quantitative CROWN-versus-IBP comparisons and runtime measurements. The separately attributed baseline curves do not negate these original results.

M1.justification: The bounded-adversary interface changes from separate feature and label budgets n and m to one budget n for affected examples. Correspondingly, aggregation selects max(m,n) contributions in v2 Theorem 3.3 versus n in v3 Theorem 3.4. The underlying SGD, interval propagation, CROWN and clipping framework remains.

E1.justification: The datasets and principal tasks remain unchanged. However, the OCT-MNIST backdoor panel changes from 'Feature + Label Poisoning' in v2 Figure 4 to 'Feature Poisoning' in v3 Figure 5 while retaining the surrounding description and curves. The PDFs do not resolve whether this corrects a caption or changes the evaluated attack scenario.

E2.justification: v2's MNIST Figure 3 reports AGT alone; v3 Figure 4 adds DPA with 3000 models and randomized smoothing, using curves reproduced from Levine and Feizi and Rosenfeld et al. v3 also adds a direct CROWN-versus-IBP comparison in Figure 3 and a runtime comparison with standard training in Table 1.

E3.justification: Several experimental grids change substantially. Figure 2 replaces widths 100/300/400 with 64/128/256 and learning rates 0.02/0.05/0.1 with 0.005/0.01/0.02, alongside revised perturbation strengths. The collision study changes attack counts from 100/500/1000 to 100/200/400. The new CROWN/IBP experiment measures final average parameter-bound width across architectures. These establish revised reported settings without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Figure 3 quantitatively isolates the effect of CROWN versus IBP on bound tightness across network depths and widths, extending v2's qualitative discussion. Existing parameter-trajectory and collision-attack illustrations are revised. The three heuristic attack studies are retained from Appendix H as Appendix E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for its experiments. The shaded certification regions represent deterministic bounds, not statistical uncertainty; the added results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds comparative accuracy, bound-width and runtime results. Its MNIST comparison reports AGT exceeding randomized smoothing only for small label-flip budgets and never exceeding DPA in the plotted comparison. Table 1 reports, for example, OCT-MNIST iteration times of 0.96 seconds for AGT versus 0.10 for standard training. Halfmoons, UCI and appendix attack plots also contain replaced results; changed settings prevent interpreting them as uniform same-setting gains.

T1.justification: v3 revises the threat-model and objective formalizations, rewrites the correctness and bounded-aggregation arguments, and adds dedicated unbounded-adversary and interval-CROWN proofs in F.3 and F.5. It removes v2's explicit interval-multiplication construction and overestimation statement. The expanded proofs are not uniformly resolved: F.3 uses intermediate sums over b terms where its replacement argument and final bound require b-n terms.

C1.justification: The central claim of certifying gradient-based training against poisoning remains. The contribution list broadens the stated proof coverage from the three named attack goals to arbitrary adversarial goals and explicitly presents the framework as a tool for analyzing other defenses and benchmarks. The abstract and conclusion otherwise retain their principal claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an empirical interpretation of runtime overhead as typically below 2× and discusses the scope and computational tradeoffs accompanying its baseline comparison. It strengthens the statement about simultaneous coordinatewise worst cases from potentially unrealizable to unrealizable by practical attacks. The principal batch-size, architecture and multiclass limitations were already present in v2.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds per-iteration timing information while retaining the hardware, code link and common hyperparameter table. Conversely, v3 omits v2's explicit identification of the PCA-based MNIST classifier as linear and abbreviates the interval-multiplication implementation recipe, removing some reproducibility detail.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gosch et al. (2024), contrasting its NTK/SVM approach and infinite-width assumption with AGT. It removes references to Nguyen (2012), Saha et al. (2020) and Weber et al. (2023), and revises the characterization of Rosenfeld et al.'s guarantees. The broader research positioning remains recognizable.

P1.justification: The background and methodology are substantially reorganized. Attack objectives move from Section 2.2 to Appendix B; descent-direction bounding gains its own subsection; interval arithmetic, CROWN, loss bounds and backward propagation are consolidated into Appendix C; proofs are regrouped in Appendix F. Extensive explanatory rewriting accompanies these moves.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a different journal layout, title/author block, typography and algorithm format. Numerous figures are resized, relocated or redrawn with revised axes, legends and captions. It adds the CROWN/IBP figure and runtime table, while renumbering retained figures and the hyperparameter table.

improvement.justification: v3 makes AGT easier to assess through explicit baseline comparisons, a quantitative CROWN/IBP ablation and measured runtime costs. These provide useful evidence about its strengths and disadvantages. The gains are tempered by errors in the expanded proof material, such as F.3's intermediate summation, and an insufficiently qualified below-2× runtime summary despite OCT-MNIST's reported 9.6× overhead.
